title: slo reservation and backoff coordinator: hotfix to prevent cascade evictions
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Production incidents in multiple regions showed rapid tenant eviction cascades during transient overloads. Root cause: the global SLO allocator was releasing reservation tokens too aggressively on circuit flips and the reopen path did not apply a coordinated exponential backoff across related resources. This PR introduces a small, targeted hotfix that (1) adds a SLO reservation layer so in-flight requests and recently-primed tenants retain a short-lived reservation buffer, (2) centralizes reopen backoff coordination between the load_shedder and the circuit state machine to avoid synchronized reopen storms, and (3) emits new telemetry (reservation_event, backoff_group) for post-mortem and alerting. Summary of changes: - Add ReserveCoordinator with namespace-aware short-lived reservations (default 250ms) that are consumed by the prioritizer before eviction - Add exponential, jittered reopen backoff that is propagated via backoff_group tags so related circuits share a dampening window - Modify load_shedder to consult reservations before marking a tenant as evictable; this reduces false positives during short bursts - Add defensive fallback: if reservation subsystem fails, system falls back to conservative eviction path to maintain safety - Wire new telemetry counters and traces: slo_reservation.acquire, slo_reservation.expire, backoff_group.enter, backoff_group.cooldown Motivation: This is a minimal change to reduce noisy cascading evictions that caused customer-impacting SLO blips. The intent is behavioral stabilization (hotfix) without changing long-term allocation policies. Testing: unit tests added for ReserveCoordinator semantics, integration test that simulates flood then short burst to ensure reservations are honored, and e2e canary run against a staging region. CI history: initial run failed due to a flaky TestCircuitReopenTiming; fixed by adding a deterministic clock injection in the test harness. Rollout plan: merged to main and will ship an immediate canary to region-eu-1 and region-na-2 for 30 minutes with telemetry thresholds watched by SRE. If any regressions, rollback via revert commit. Backport: none (hotfix targeted for main and immediate canary). Checklist: [x] Adds unit/integration tests [x] Telemetry + dashboards updated [x] SRE reviewed revert/rollout steps [x] No schema/DB migrations Risks: small latency increase for admission path (~250us median) and a risk of slightly delayed eviction under sustained heavy overload; mitigated by conservative fallbacks. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-11402, SRE-487.
